Build a signed systemd-boot A/B release with a verified root from a prepared
Debian root filesystem.

## Inputs

<dl class="reference-list">

<dt>

`rootfs`

</dt>
<dd>

Kind: directory

**Required**

Prepared root filesystem implementing the core verified-root boot contract.

</dd>

<dt>

`boot-certificate`

</dt>
<dd>

Kind: file

**Required**

PEM-encoded RSA X.509 certificate for signing EFI boot artifacts.

</dd>

<dt>

`bundle-certificate`

</dt>
<dd>

Kind: file

**Required**

Single PEM-encoded X.509 end-entity signer certificate issued directly by the
trusted root. No intermediates. The default signer requires RSA.

</dd>

<dt>

`secure-boot-keys`

</dt>
<dd>

Kind: directory

Default: `{"tree":{}}`

Authenticated variables PK.auth, KEK.auth, and db.auth that systemd-boot enrolls
in Setup Mode. Empty by default, disabling enrollment.

</dd>

</dl>

## Parameters

<dl class="reference-list">

<dt>

`architecture`

</dt>
<dd>

**Required**

Target architecture: amd64 or arm64. Must match the system architecture.

</dd>

<dt>

`kernel-version`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `""`

Exact installed kernel version. Empty selects the unique installed version.

</dd>

<dt>

`cmdline-extra`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `""`

Additional authenticated kernel arguments.

</dd>

<dt>

`panic-timeout`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `10`

Kernel panic reboot delay in seconds. Zero leaves the system stopped.

</dd>

<dt>

`boot-timeout`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `0`

systemd-boot menu timeout in seconds.

</dd>

<dt>

`signing-time`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `""`

Signing time as Unix seconds in a string. Empty uses the build source epoch.

</dd>

<dt>

`config-size`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `0`

ESP capacity in bytes. Zero reserves three copies of its current files, uses at
least 256 MiB, and rounds up to 64 MiB.

</dd>

<dt>

`root-compression`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `"none"`

SquashFS compression of the root filesystem, such as zstd or xz, or none.

</dd>

<dt>

`disk-size`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `0`

Factory disk capacity in bytes. Zero sizes the disk from its partitions.

</dd>

<dt>

`secondary-config`

</dt>
<dd>

Default: `false`

Reserve an empty secondary configuration partition with the same capacity as the
ESP.

</dd>

</dl>

## Rule Parameters

Callers can replace these operations through `rules` bindings. An implementation
receives the listed inputs and parameters and must produce the listed outputs.
See [Rule Parameters](/docs/bakery/next/build-rules#rule-parameters).

### `efi-signer`

Sign an EFI executable. Bakery verifies each signature against boot-certificate.

Default implementation: `core/sign-efi`.

<dl class="reference-list">

<dt>

Input `image`

</dt>
<dd>

Kind: file

Unsigned PE executable: the UKI or systemd-boot.

</dd>

<dt>

Input `certificate`

</dt>
<dd>

Kind: file

The boot-certificate input.

</dd>

<dt>

Parameter `signing-time`

</dt>
<dd>

Signing time as Unix seconds in a string. Empty means the build source epoch.

</dd>

<dt>

Output `image`

</dt>
<dd>

Kind: file

PE executable with a UEFI Secure Boot signature.

</dd>

</dl>

### `bundle-signer`

Create a CMS signature over the bundle's signed metadata. Bakery verifies it
against bundle-certificate.

Default implementation: `core/sign-cms`.

<dl class="reference-list">

<dt>

Input `content`

</dt>
<dd>

Kind: file

Signed bundle metadata.

</dd>

<dt>

Input `certificate`

</dt>
<dd>

Kind: file

The bundle-certificate input.

</dd>

<dt>

Parameter `signing-time`

</dt>
<dd>

Signing time as Unix seconds in a string. Empty means the build source epoch.

</dd>

<dt>

Output `signature`

</dt>
<dd>

Kind: file

DER-encoded CMS SignedData with the encapsulated content and signer certificate.

</dd>

</dl>

## Execution

Composes other rules into a build graph.

## Behavior

Build an EFI A/B release with a verified root from a prepared Debian root
filesystem. This wrapper selects one installed kernel with `core/kernel-debian`,
generates its initrd with `core/initrd-debian`, and passes both to
[`core/image-efi-verified`](../image-efi-verified/).

Prepare the root filesystem with
[`core/debian-efi-verified-setup`](../../recipes/debian-efi-verified-setup/) and
configure trusted update signers in `/etc/rugix/ctrl.toml` through a project
recipe. On first boot, Rugix Ctrl completes the factory layout through native
bootstrap. The wrapper consumes the prepared root without modifying it.

The required `architecture` must match the system's `architecture` setting. Set
`kernel-version` when several installed kernels exist; its empty default
requires a unique installed kernel. Automatic capacity defaults, optional size
overrides, remaining release inputs, signing policy, outputs, and
[Secure Boot key enrollment](../image-efi-verified/#enroll-secure-boot-keys)
match the generic EFI composition. The wrapper forwards its `efi-signer` and
`bundle-signer` rule parameters to it, so you can sign with an HSM or a KMS as
described in [its signer documentation](../image-efi-verified/#signers).

## Customize Boot Settings

Set `cmdline-extra` to supply kernel arguments, such as consoles and log levels.
It defaults to an empty string. The `panic-timeout` parameter defaults to 10
seconds; zero disables automatic reboot after a panic. Verified-root arguments
remain supplied by the composition.

Set `boot-timeout` to control the systemd-boot menu timeout in seconds. For
example:

```toml
parameters.cmdline-extra = "console=ttyS0,115200n8 loglevel=4"
parameters.panic-timeout = 30
parameters.boot-timeout = 5
```

## Example

For example, select the wrapper in a system definition:

```toml
[systems.efi]
layer = "efi"
architecture = "amd64"

[systems.efi.rules.release]
uses = "core/image-debian-efi-verified"
parameters.architecture = "amd64"
inputs.boot-certificate = { path = "keys/boot.crt" }
inputs.bundle-certificate = { path = "keys/bundle.crt" }
rules.efi-signer.secrets.key = { path = "keys/boot.key" }
rules.bundle-signer.secrets.key = { path = "keys/bundle.key" }

[systems.efi.outputs]
"system.img" = { rule = { node = "release", output = "image" } }
"system.rugixb" = { rule = { node = "release", output = "bundle" } }
"system.rugixb-hash" = { rule = { node = "release", output = "bundle-hash" } }
```

Bakery supplies the built layer as `rootfs`. Run
`./run-bakery bake system efi --release-version v1`.

## Secondary Configuration Partition

To reserve space for a replacement ESP, including systemd-boot, set
`parameters.secondary-config = true`. This adds an empty `config-secondary`
partition with the same capacity as `config`. Both config partitions precede the
system partitions, so `system-a`, `system-b`, and `data` use partition numbers
3, 4, and 5 after bootstrap.

Enable the matching recipe option in the root filesystem's layer:

```toml
[parameters."core/debian-efi-verified-setup"]
secondary_config = true
```

Use this option when provisioning a matching factory layout. Existing
installations need a separate partition-layout migration before receiving the
changed root configuration.

Custom roots must provide equivalent system and bootstrap configurations. The
[EFI layout rule](../layout-efi-ab/) describes the reserved partition. The
update bundle continues to update the root and UKI slots; updating and
activating a replacement ESP requires a separate operation.
